keyFindings.description: Await keeps an observation error in `failed` and reports it only when ctx ends. Its long-lived callers therefore wait forever, with nothing logged, while every observation fails: the hub seed (delivery_live_hub_intake.go:123, on the hub's lifetime, so the retry log at :135 never fires), the relay's first start (event_stream_relay.go:210, where a resuming stream heartbeats but carries no events), and the relay reseed after a reset. Main logged a failed cursor read (readCursors) and returned start's error to the SSE handler. A plausible trigger: the horizon pool's 2 connections cannot dial while the shared pool's existing connections keep working. This hides an error, so it is fixed in this pull request: log observation failures the caller's ctx did not cause, rate-limited like the stall warning.

A cold stream that has not opened sends no bytes. The browser's 45 s watchdog (sse.ts:80-86) then aborts and reconnects it cold, with backoff up to 30 s, for as long as a stall holds on a newly started process. No event is lost. Name this interaction and its bound in the handler comment.

The stall diagnosis derives its context with context.WithoutCancel(ctx), so it keeps the caller's store hold mark. In the shared-pool fallback it can be refused (nested acquire), and since it now runs concurrently it can block the caller's next read. Derive it from context.Background().

The subscribe goroutine is detached from the handler (events.go awaitEventSubscription), so a start that finishes after the server's lifetime ends can call r.running.Add(2) concurrently with or after waitBackground's Wait. That Add/Wait ordering is one the race detector reports. Check the lifetime under mu before Add, or track the goroutine.

The seed goroutine sends to h.seeds without a select. It cannot block only because no second seed starts while one runs, and that rule is kept in other functions. Make the send select on h.lifetime.Done().
